speaker: Doctor
text: I cannot diagnose a migraine in a 2-day-old infant presenting with bilious vomiting and abdominal distension, as this is a surgical emergency likely indicative of Hirschsprung disease or malrotation. I must request further imaging or tests to identify the correct cause. REQUEST TEST: Contrast Enema

speaker: Doctor
text: A normal abdominal X-ray and contrast enema are highly unusual for this presentation, so I need to rule out other causes like meconium plug syndrome or small left colon syndrome. REQUEST TEST: Rectal Biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Absence of ganglion cells in the submucosa and myenteric plexus, consistent with Hirschsprung’s disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: The absence of ganglion cells in the rectal biopsy is diagnostic for Hirschsprung's disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung's disease
